# ACC004 `reduction-into-device-module-variable`

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

An OpenACC `reduction` targets a module allocatable declared `!$acc declare create`.

## Why

A reduction whose target is a module allocatable made device-resident by `!$acc declare create`
fails with nvfortran (the kernel does not launch or the result is wrong), while the same code
works with a local variable. Reduce into a local scalar and assign it to the module variable
afterwards.

## Reported

```fortran
module state
  real, allocatable :: total
  !$acc declare create(total)
...
!$acc parallel loop reduction(+:total)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
real :: partial
partial = 0.0
!$acc parallel loop reduction(+:partial)
...
total = partial
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[ACC004] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = ACC004` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).
